forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cheltenham council to fall £563,000 short of minimum reserves by March
news_drafts.lead: Cheltenham's general reserves are forecast to fall to £937,000 by 31 March 2027, leaving the council £563,000 below the level its Section 151 Officer, the chief finance officer, assesses as prudent. An £838,000 forecast overspend is the cause. At the same time, the council's capital programme — money spent on long-lived assets such as buildings — is being cut by 13.5%, from £42.96m to £37.1m. The National Cyber Innovation Centre at Golden Valley, budgeted at £32.85m, is unaffected and now represents 89 per cent of the entire capital spending plan. Separately, the Housing Revenue Account, which manages council housing and is funded by rents, is forecast to overspend by £650,000, driven by £465,000 in lost rental income from vacant properties and £201,000 in additional borrowing costs from higher interest rates.

findings.paper_title: Quarterly Budget Management Report 2026-27 position at 31 October 2026
findings.headline: The Government has announced ringfenced rough sleeping funding, with Cheltenham expected to receive approximately £256,000 in 2026/27
findings.detail: The report says the funding is expected to reduce the need to use existing Homelessness Prevention Grant for new initiatives, and that homelessness prevention investment decisions have been delayed pending countywide funding discussions from 2027/28.
findings.matters: Ringfenced grant that replaces core-funded spend is a common way councils manage homelessness costs, and the report links it to a deferral of future commitments.
findings.quote: with Cheltenham expected to receive approximately £256,000 during 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Quarterly Budget Management Report 2026-27 position at 31 October 2026
findings.headline: Elections and Electoral Registration is forecast £148,000 adverse after the Government decided to proceed with the local elections, with the Elections Reserve already used
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget assumed the elections would be cancelled under local government reorganisation proposals. The Elections Reserve had been used previously and was not available to offset the costs.
findings.matters: Councils whose reorganisation assumptions change can see how a budget set on one basis is affected when the decision reverses, and how reserve draw-downs leave less cover.
findings.quote: Following the Government's subsequent decision to proceed with the elections, the service has incurred costs that were not reflected within the approved budget.

findings.paper_title: Quarterly Budget Management Report 2026-27 position at 31 October 2026
findings.headline: Business rates collection is at 60.86% against a 58.10% target, with business rates arrears at £1.152m against a £1.300m target
findings.detail: Council tax collection is 56.24% against a 56.30% profiled target, with council tax arrears at £3.577m against a £3.500m target. The report says business rates arrears have fallen from £1.774m a year earlier.
findings.matters: Collection Fund performance affects future-year funding, and councils can compare their own collection rates and arrears trends with the same reporting period.
findings.figures: 60.86% business rates collected; 58.10% target; £1.152m business rates arrears; £1.300m target; 56.24% council tax collected; £3.577m council tax arrears
findings.quote: Business Rates collection performance continues to be strong, with 60.86% of annual charges collected at 30 September 2026, exceeding the profiled target of 58.10%

findings.paper_title: Quarterly Budget Management Report 2026-27 position at 31 October 2026
findings.headline: The HRA capital programme is forecast at £19.27m against an approved budget of £43.33m, with £24.06m slipping into future years
findings.detail: The report attributes slippage to the timing of project delivery, procurement and contractual milestones on major schemes. The largest current-year items are the retrofit programme, 320 Swindon Road and Monkscroft School.
findings.matters: A council's HRA development and stock investment plans can slip against approved budgets, and peers can compare the scale of the slippage.
findings.figures: £43.33m approved budget; £19.27m forecast expenditure; £24.06m slippage; £4.65m retrofit; £4.31m 320 Swindon Road; £0.73m Monkscroft School
findings.quote: the HRA Capital Programme has an approved budget of £43.33m for 2026/27, with forecast expenditure of £19.27m, resulting in projected slippage of approximately £24.06m into future years.

findings.paper_title: Quarterly Budget Management Report 2026-27 position at 31 October 2026
findings.headline: The General Fund capital programme is forecast at £30.90m against an adjusted budget of £36.81m, with £5.91m slipping into future years
findings.detail: The report attributes most planned spend to the National Cyber Innovation Centre (Golden Valley Development). The review of the expenditure profile is not expected to change the overall approved project budget. Officers are also reviewing the wider programme for affordability.
findings.matters: A finance director can compare how much of the capital budget is slipping and whether a large regeneration scheme is affecting the phasing of the programme.
findings.quote: the General Fund Capital Programme has an adjusted budget of £36.81m for 2026/27, with forecast expenditure of £30.90m, resulting in projected slippage of approximately £5.91m into future years.

daily_post.headline: Gloucestershire business rates pooling arrangement not financially beneficial following baseline reset
daily_post.lead: Business rates pooling can be a material income source where growth is available; the reset has eliminated this benefit, removing a potential income offset to budget pressures.
